items.entity: square design domain (physical size and out-of-plane thickness)
items.description: Sec. 4.6 'Square Domain Study' only says 'a standard square design domain'; no side length, element size or plate thickness is given, and the reported compliance 5.0506 has no units.
readings: 64 x 64 length units (unit-size elements), unit thickness
Physical bracket size (e.g., 200 mm x 200 mm) with a chosen plate thickness

items.entity: grid resolution of the square domain
items.description: Case 1 does not state its resolution. 'Standard' presumably means the 64x64 TopoDiff dataset grid used by the pretrained model (Sec. 4.7.3; Table 8; App. C.1 'k=64 for the 64x64 design domain'). It is not stated explicitly whether 64x64 counts elements or nodes, or which element type is used.
readings: 64 x 64 square bilinear (Q4) elements, 65 x 65 nodes
64 x 64 nodes, i.e., 63 x 63 Q4 elements

items.entity: wall-attachment supports of the shelf bracket
items.description: The text gives no support location for case 1, only 'shelf bracket' and the Fig. 6 caption. A wall-side edge is implied. Whether the whole edge or only screw points/patches are restrained, and whether this is one of the 42 training or 5 OOD dataset BCs (Sec. 4.1), is shown only in Fig. 6.
readings: Entire left (wall) edge restrained, y/H from 0 to 1
Two short patches at the ends of the left edge (e.g., y/H in [0,0.1] and [0.9,1.0]) representing screws
Only the top-left and bottom-left corner nodes restrained
Upper half of the left edge restrained (y/H in [0.5,1.0])

items.entity: wall-attachment supports of the shelf bracket
items.description: Which displacement components (x, y or both) are fixed is not stated. Supports are only called 'constrained boundary supports' (Sec. 4.1, App. E).
readings: All support nodes fixed in x and y (clamped)
Upper attachment fixed in x and y, lower attachment fixed in x only (bearing against wall)
Wall edge fixed in x only plus one node fixed in y

items.description: The load location is not given. The dataset rule only says loads act at unconstrained boundary nodes (Sec. 4.1). With the wall at x=0 and the shelf on the top edge, the application point is shown only in Fig. 6.
readings: Top-right corner node (x/L = 1.0, y/H = 1.0), free tip of the arm

items.description: The direction is not stated. Dataset loads take angles in [0, pi] in pi/6 steps (Sec. 4.1), with no reference axis given. Gravity suggests vertical (the sign does not matter for compliance), but an inclined dataset direction cannot be ruled out without Fig. 6.
readings: Vertical, perpendicular to the top edge (pi/2, i.e. gravity/downward)

items.description: The benchmark uses a single load at one boundary node (Sec. 4.1; Sec. 4.7.3 'single-load cases'). However, Secs. 3.3 and 4.7.3 refer to a 'load region', and a real shelf applies a distributed load. Case 1 does not say which applies.
readings: Uniformly distributed load along the full top edge
Load spread over a short patch (a few nodes) at the tip

items.description: No load magnitude is given anywhere (Sec. 4.1, 4.6); only the resulting compliance of 5.0506 is reported.
readings: Another value, e.g., a physical shelf weight in N

items.entity: prescribed volume fraction v_f of case 1
items.description: Sec. 4.6 does not give v_f for the shelf bracket. Only the dataset range, 0.3 to 0.5 in 0.02 steps (Sec. 4.1), is known.

The text is silent on passive regions for case 1. The model inputs (BCs, load, v_f, physics fields) include no passive-region channel, but a shelf-bracket design could include solid flanges or a void envelope that only Fig. 6 would show.
readings: Solid non-design strip along the top edge (shelf seat)
Solid non-design strip along the wall edge (mounting plate)
Void non-design triangle in the lower-right corner

items.description: No elastic modulus is given for the SIMP reference or the FEA evaluation (Sec. 3.1, 4.1, 4.2, 4.6).
Neither nu nor the choice of plane stress or plane strain is stated. Sec. 4.2 only says 'a standard FEA solver'.
The ground truth is 'obtained by SIMP' (Sec. 4.6) and the dataset was 'collected using the SIMP method' (Sec. 4.1), but the penalty exponent p is never given.
readings: p = 3 reached by continuation from p = 1

items.description: No filter type or radius is given for the SIMP reference design (Sec. 4.1, 4.6).

items.entity: SIMP optimizer, initial design and stopping rule
items.description: The update scheme, starting design and convergence or iteration limit of the SIMP run are not given. Table 8 only reports a 23.93 s CPU run.
readings: OC (move 0.2, eta = 0.5), uniform start x = v_f, stop when max density change < 0.01

items.description: Eq. (1) states 0 < x_min <= x <= 1 but gives no value. x_min sets the void stiffness in the SIMP run and in the compliance re-analysis.

items.entity: compliance evaluation of the SIMP reference (5.0506)
items.description: Sec. 4.2 evaluates all metrics on designs binarized at tau = 0.5 with a standard FEA solver. Sec. 4.6 does not say whether 5.0506 is the compliance of the grey-scale SIMP design or of the thresholded, re-analysed design.
readings: Compliance of the converged grey-scale SIMP density field
Compliance of the SIMP design thresholded at 0.5 and re-analysed (void at x_min)
